semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {قُلْ هُوَ الله أَحَدٌ}: concerning «هو» there are two views. The first: it is a pronoun referring back to what is understood from the context, for it is related in the occasions of revelation that they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Describe your Lord to us and give His lineage." It was also said: they said to him: "Is He of copper or of iron?" — so it was revealed. On this view «الله» may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أَحَدٌ» its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of the first [«هو»]. «اللَّهُ» may also be a badal (substitute) with «أحدٌ» the khabar; or «اللَّهُ» a first khabar and «أحدٌ» a second khabar; or «أحدٌ» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is One". The second: it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), because it is a place of magnification, and the clause after it is its explanatory khabar.
The hamza of «أحد» is substituted for a wāw, because it is from al-waḥda (oneness); and the substitution of hamza for a wāw with fatḥa [Translator's note: the sentence is left incomplete in the source; the sense is that such a substitution is rare]. It was said: from it is "imraʾa anāh" (a deliberate, slow woman), from al-wanā, which is languor. The difference was given before between this «أحد» and the «أحد» meant for generality, for the hamza of that one is itself original. Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted that the hamza of this «أحد» is not changed, but is itself original, like the one meant for generality; but the well-known view is the first. Thaʿlab distinguished between «واحد» and «أحد»: wāḥid admits counting, the plural and the dual, whereas aḥad does not admit that; one says "Allah is aḥad" but one does not say "Zayd is aḥad", because Allah the Exalted has this exclusive quality, whereas Zayd has various states. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this from him: "One says aḥad wa-ʿishrūn (twenty-one) and the like, so counting does enter it." — end of quote. Makkī said: "aḥad was originally waḥad; the wāw was changed into hamza, so two alifs came together, because the hamza resembles the alif; so one of them was dropped for lightness." [Translator's note: so in the source.]
ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and Ubayy read {اللَّهُ أحدٌ} without «قُلْ». The Prophet ﷺ read «أحدٌ» without «قل هو». Al-Aʿmash read: «قل هو اللَّهُ الواحد».
The generality read «أحدٌ» with tanwīn, which is the original. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abān ibn ʿUthmān, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-Ḥasan, Abū al-Sammāl, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, among a great number, read it with the tanwīn dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in his saying:
4675 - عمرُو الذي هَشَمَ الثَّريدَ لقومِه ... ورجالُ مكةَ مُسْنِتُون عِجافُ
(ʿAmr, who crumbled bread into broth for his people when the men of Mecca were famine-struck and emaciated.)
Another said:
4676 - فأَلْفَيْتُه غيرَ مُسْتَعْتِبٍ ... ولا ذاكرَ اللَّهَ إلاَّ قليلا
(I found him not seeking to make amends, nor remembering Allah except a little.)

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {الصمد}: on the pattern faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl, like al-qabaḍ and al-naqaḍ. He is the master to whom one turns (yuṣmadu ilayhi) in needs, i.e. who is sought, and none is able to fulfil them except Him. The following was recited:
4677 - ألا بَكَّرَ النَّاعي بخَيْرِ بني أسدْ ... بعَمْرِو بن مسعودٍ وبالسَّيِّد الصَّمَدْ
(Lo, the announcer of death came early with [news of] the best of Banū Asad — ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd, the master to whom all turned.)
Another said:
4678 - عَلَوْتُه بحُسامٍ ثم قُلْتُ له ... خُذْها حُذَيْفُ فأنتَ السَّيِّدُ الصَّمَدُ
(I came down on him with a sharp sword, then said to him: "Take it, Ḥudhayf, for you are the master to whom all turn.")
It was also said: al-ṣamad is that which has no hollow; from it is his saying:
4679 - شِهابُ حُروبٍ لا تَزال جيادُه ... عوابِسَ يَعْلُكْنَ الشَّكِيْمَ المُصَمَّدا
(A blazing star of wars, whose steeds are ever grim-faced, champing on the solid bit.)
Ibn Kaʿb said: its explanation is what follows it, namely His saying «لم يَلِدْ ولم يُوْلَدُ»; this resembles what they said in explaining al-halūʿ. The best [view] of this clause is that it is independent, with the benefit of this predication. «الصَّمَدُ» may also be an adjective, with the khabar (predicate) being in the clause after it; so it was said, but it is weak from the standpoint of the context, for the context requires each clause to be independent in its predication.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {كُفُواً أَحَدٌ}: concerning its accusative there are two views. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of «يكنْ», «أحدٌ» is its noun (ism), and «له» is attached to the khabar, i.e. "and none is equal to Him". Al-Mubarrad objected to Sībawayh with this verse, inasmuch as he [Sībawayh] claims that when the adverbial phrase (ẓarf) is placed first it is the khabar, whereas here He did not make it the khabar despite its being placed first.
Al-Mubarrad was answered in two ways. The first: Sībawayh did not make that obligatory, but only permitted it. The second: we do not concede that the adverbial phrase here is not a khabar; rather it is the khabar, and «كُفُواً» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as will be explained. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Eloquent Arabic speech is to postpone the adverbial phrase that is laghw (dependent, not standing as a predicate) and not mustaqarr, and not to place it first; Sībawayh stated this explicitly in his Kitāb. So why is it placed first in the most eloquent and purest speech? I say: this discourse was brought only to negate equivalence from the essence of the Creator, exalted is He, and the focus and centre of this meaning is this adverbial phrase; so for that reason it was the most important, the most relevant, and the most deserving and worthy of being placed first."
The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl from «أحد», because it was its adjective, and when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl, and «له» is the khabar; Makkī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and others said this. It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun latent (mustakinn) in the prepositional phrase, since it occurs as khabar. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān], after relating the words of al-Zamakhsharī and Makkī, said: "This clause is not of this category, because in His saying {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ} the preposition and its genitive noun are not complete (tāmm); it is only incomplete (nāqiṣ), not fit to be the khabar of «كان»; rather it is attached to «كُفُواً» and placed before it. The implied form is: 'and none is equivalent to Him'. So it is in the sense of the object, attached to «كُفُواً», and was placed before «كُفُواً» because of concern for it, since it contains the pronoun of the Creator, exalted is He. And the khabar was placed in the middle, even though its origin is to be postponed, because the postponed noun is a verse-ending (fāṣila), so that was fitting.
On the basis of what we have established, the parsing of Makkī and others — that «له» is the khabar and «كُفُواً» a ḥāl from «أحد» — is void, because it is an incomplete adverbial phrase not fit to be a khabar. By that al-Zamakhsharī's question and answer are also void. Sībawayh spoke only of the adverbial phrase that is fit to be a khabar or not to be. Sībawayh said: 'You say: «ما كان فيها أحدٌ خيرٌ منك», «وما كان [أحدٌ] مثلُك فيها», and «ليس أحدٌ فيها خيرٌ منك», when you make «فيها» mustaqarr (predicative) and do not construe it as in your saying «فيها زيدٌ قائمٌ»: you make the adjective follow the noun. If you construe it as «فيها زيدٌ قائمٌ», you use the accusative and say: «ما كان فيها أحدٌ خيراً منك» and «وما كان أحدٌ خيراً منك فيها». Except that when you intend cancellation (ilghāʾ), the further you postpone what is cancelled the better; and when you intend it to be mustaqarr, the further forward you place it the better. Placing first, postponing, cancellation and predication are all good, frequent Arabic. The Exalted said: {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ}, and the poet said:
4680 - ما دامَ فيهِنَّ فَصِيْلٌ حَيَّاً ...
(As long as there is among them a weaned young camel alive…)'
— end of Sībawayh's words." The Shaykh said: "You see his words and his illustration with the adverbial phrase that is fit to be a khabar. The meaning of his saying 'mustaqarr' is: a khabar of the mubtadaʾ or of kāna. If you say: but he gave the verse as an example — I say: this is what led Makkī, al-Zamakhsharī and others into what they fell into. Sībawayh only meant that the complete adverbial phrase, which is in his saying:
ما دامَ فيهِنَّ فَصِيلٌ حَيَّاً ...
is treated as an extra element (faḍla), not as a khabar, just as «له» in the verse is treated as an extra element; so he made the adverbial phrase that could be a khabar like the incomplete adverbial phrase in not being used as a khabar. No one with a sound mind doubts that no statement is formed from «له أحد»; indeed, if «كُفُو» were postponed and made nominative as an adjective while «له» was made the khabar, no statement would be formed from it. Rather you see that the negation applies only to the khabar, which is «كُفُواً», and the meaning is: none is equivalent to Him." — end of what the Shaykh said.
His saying "no one doubts…" to its end is an attempt to overawe the reader. Otherwise his saying "this adverbial phrase is incomplete" is not conceded, because the incomplete adverbial phrase refers to one in whose predication there is no benefit, like one cut off from annexation, and like «في دارٍ رجلٌ». He transmitted from Sībawayh the preceding examples, such as «ما كان فيها أحدٌ خيراً منك» — and what is the difference between this and the noble verse? And how can he say this when Sībawayh said at the end of his words: "Placing first, postponing, cancellation and predication are all good, frequent Arabic"?
The generality read with ḍamma on the kāf and the fāʾ [«كُفُؤاً»]. Al-Aʿraj, Shayba and Nāfiʿ in one transmission eased (sahhala) the hamza. Ḥamza made the fāʾ quiescent [«كُفْؤاً»] and changed the hamza into wāw in pause only. Ḥafṣ changed it into wāw in all cases. The rest read with hamza in all cases. Discussion of this was given at the beginning of al-Baqara at His saying: {هُزُواً} [al-Baqara: 67].
Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās read «كِفاءٌ» with kasra and lengthening, i.e. He has no like. The following by al-Nābigha was recited:
4681 - لا تَقْذِفَنِّي برُكْنٍ لا كِفاءَ له ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Do not hurl at me a force [lit. a pillar] that has no equal…)
Nāfiʿ, in one transmission, read «كِفا» with kasra and fatḥa on the fāʾ, without lengthening, as though he transferred the vowel of the hamza and dropped it. Al-kufʾ: the counterpart; "this is a kufʾ for you", i.e. your counterpart; the noun is al-kafāʾa, with fatḥa.
